_what: Eye-verified census of arcade enemy-aircraft APPEARANCES. An appearance is counted when the aircraft is absent in one sampled frame and present <=0.167 s later (6 Hz census sheets; one entry resolved at 60 Hz). Fields: [t_seconds, entry_region, first_visible_DRAWN_width_pctW, note]. entry_region is where the sprite first appears: TOP/LEFT/RIGHT/BOTTOM = touching that screen edge; INTERIOR = fully inside the frame.
_operator: DRAWN width = sprite bbox width / 1028 px, read off the 2 %W grid baked into the native-resolution frame (judging/R40/density-truth/gridframe.py) or off the blob bbox where the aircraft is over clean sky. Widths of edge-clipped arrivals are the VISIBLE width and are therefore lower bounds on the true span.
_bias: Built by resolving appearances on 0.46-scale 6 Hz sheets. Specks below ~2 %W are ~5 px in a tile and are UNDER-counted here; the speck population is characterised instead by the 2 Hz full-frame read in handread.json (sky is 'specks only' 8.5 % of the time). Read the >=8 %W share as: of the appearances a player would register, this fraction is ALREADY large on arrival.
_rejected_instrument: track.py's 60 Hz tracker produced candidate arrivals automatically, but filmstrip inspection showed two of its longest 'growth' tracks (s4 id1176, id2469) had drifted onto the HUD SCORE/HIT plates, and another (id265) was an expanding explosion. No tracker-derived arrival figure is published.
